raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was 21. Thirty-five years teaches you things no school can. My fields know me and I know them. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

My 12.4 mu splits naturally — about 7 mu goes into the wheat-maize rotation, and I keep 5.4 mu in cotton. Cotton is hard on the body and hard to find pickers for now that my son and daughter-in-law are in the city, but the price is still better than grain so I keep it.

**Wheat:** I'll plant Jimai variety again — it did well last two years, and the village seed station always has it. Rotary till after the maize harvest in October, then plant mid-October. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and push urea at jointing. Three irrigations — before freeze, jointing, and heading. Two pesticide sprays: one for aphids in spring, one fungicide at heading because last year there was some rust.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I go straight in with no-till — saves moisture and I don't need to hire a tractor. Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed from the market, reliable and I know the yield. Two irrigations if July is dry — tasseling is critical. One spray for fall armyworm if I see it.

**Cotton:** Plant late April. Bt cotton seed, same supplier as last three years. More irrigation needed — at least four times. Still spray four times for aphids and spider mites even with Bt. Plough before planting to break up the hardpan. Picking will be hard with less family around, but I'll manage.

I'm not changing much from last year. What works, works.
